html:
The first coup in Ivory Coast, on 24 December 1999, when soldiers led by General Robert Guei overthrew President Henri Konan Bedie, successor of Houphouet-Boigny.

Bedie had promoted ivoirite, an idea of true Ivorian identity that cast doubt on northerners and the children of migrants, and used it to keep the northern leader Alassane Ouattara out of the election. Guei kept Ouattara out too. In the October 2000 election Guei tried to claim victory, but street protests forced him out and Laurent Gbagbo took power. Killings of northerners followed. The quarrel over who is Ivorian led straight to the civil war of 2002. See also cocoa.
sum: The first coup in Ivory Coast, on 24 December 1999, when soldiers led by General Robert Guei overthrew President Henri Konan Bedie, successor of Houphouet-Boigny.
